name: Structuring / Smurfing
description: Breaking up cash or other value into amounts kept below reporting, identification or internal review thresholds, often using many deposits, branches, accounts or individuals. It is mainly a placement technique and is commonly paired with rapid onward movement of funds.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering Typologies and Methods (general placement guidance)
FinCEN, Guidance on structuring and Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) reporting (general)
AUSTRAC, Guidance on structuring and threshold transaction reports (general)

exposure.rationale: Sub-threshold cash deposits across branches, ATMs and agents.

indicators.name: Repeated cash deposits just below reporting threshold
indicators.canon: Cash deposits just below reporting or identification threshold
indicators.desc: Repeated cash deposits kept just under a reporting, identification or monitoring threshold.
indicators.ctx: Multiple cash deposits or exchanges sized just under a regulatory reporting or internal review threshold over a short period.
indicators.fp: Customers with stable habits (e.g. fixed daily takings or standard float sizes) can legitimately generate similar amounts.

indicators.name: Same-day deposits across multiple branches or ATMs
indicators.canon: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts
indicators.desc: Cash is deposited in several locations, channels or accounts on the same day or over a short period so that no single deposit stands out.
indicators.ctx: Cash is paid in at several branches, ATMs or agents within hours, with total value well above the amount at any one location.
indicators.fp: Travelling workers or customers with several workplaces may use many locations.

indicators.name: Multiple depositors paying into one account
indicators.canon: Many unrelated depositors paying into one account
indicators.desc: Numerous unconnected individuals make deposits into the same account, often in similar amounts or within short windows.
indicators.ctx: Several unrelated individuals make cash deposits into the same account, often in similar amounts and at similar times.
indicators.fp: Collections for clubs, rent, fundraising or family contributions may fit.

indicators.name: Rapid onward movement after cash credits
indicators.canon: Rapid onward movement after cash credits
indicators.desc: Cash deposited is quickly withdrawn or transferred onward, including to another location or to unhosted wallets.
indicators.ctx: Funds credited in cash are quickly transferred out, withdrawn elsewhere or used for purchases leaving a low balance.
indicators.fp: Customers paying bills or suppliers on receipt of cash may do the same.

indicators.name: Customer reacts to reporting or ID requirements
indicators.canon: Customer reacts to reporting or ID requirements
indicators.desc: Customer reduces a transaction, splits it, or leaves when asked for ID, source of funds or told a report may be filed.
indicators.ctx: Customer reduces a transaction, splits it, or leaves when asked for ID, source of funds or told a report may be filed.
indicators.fp: Privacy concerns or lack of documents with the customer may explain some cases.

indicators.name: Deposit volumes inconsistent with customer profile
indicators.canon: Account activity inconsistent with declared occupation or income
indicators.desc: Turnover or volumes materially exceed what the customer's declared occupation, income, age or circumstances would support.
indicators.ctx: Cash volumes far exceed expected activity for the customer's declared occupation, income or business.
indicators.fp: Windfalls, asset sales or seasonal income may be genuine.

indicators.name: Frequent purchase of monetary instruments in small amounts
indicators.canon: Frequent purchase of monetary instruments in small amounts
indicators.desc: Multiple money orders, drafts, prepaid cards or cheques purchased with cash in sub-threshold amounts.
indicators.ctx: Multiple money orders, drafts, prepaid cards or cheques purchased with cash in sub-threshold amounts.
indicators.fp: Some customers lack bank accounts and use instruments for rent or bills.

indicators.name: Currency denomination or condition anomalies
indicators.desc: Cash arrives in unusual bundles, rubber-banded small notes, or mixed denominations inconsistent with the stated source.
indicators.ctx: Cash arrives in unusual bundles, rubber-banded small notes, or mixed denominations inconsistent with the stated source.
indicators.fp: Retail cash is often in small notes; condition varies by source.
